policy.purpose: Record non-identifying field observations used to validate already-admitted Photography Opportunities and runtime behavior.
policy.admission_boundary: Field observations may validate or calibrate runtime behavior but do not by themselves admit a new Place-specific subject. Subject admission remains governed by RESEARCH_EVIDENCE_SPEC_R4_2.md.
policy.privacy_boundary: Do not commit a user-supplied image by default. Store structured observation metadata only unless explicit publication permission is provided.
policy.forecast_boundary: Captured forecast values are historical validation snapshots. They must not be presented as current forecasts.

camera_direction.note: User explicitly stated the photograph was taken from Qixingtan looking north.

source.note: The photograph was reviewed in the originating conversation. The image itself is not stored in this repository.

observed_scene.interpretation: Clear/readable coast and sea with a terrain-attached cloud band on the northward mountain sector; ridges remained partially visible.

photographic_interpretation.note: The field case supports separating a readable mountain-seascape from the more specific attached-cloud-band condition.

captured_forecast_snapshot.source: ChaseLights production weather output after B85 refresh

tw-036-P03.rationale: The observed cloud band should not be a hard false negative, but grid-unresolved proxy evidence must remain explicitly uncertain.

tw-036-P04.rationale: The broad northward mountain-seascape was clearly photographable even though the local attached cloud shape was below direct grid resolution.

verification.note: B85 production replay changed the 13:00 interpretation from the earlier sunrise-only coverage failure to P04=86 medium-confidence mountain-seascape plus P03=78 low-confidence orographic-cloud candidate.

limitations: One positive field case is insufficient to estimate false-positive rate.
The LCL value is a planning proxy derived from temperature/dew point, not an observed cloud base.
Northward weather samples are environmental proxies, not exact ridge or cloud locations.
The observation validates this scene and model behavior, not a universal threshold for all mountain-cloud subjects.
